Jay Leno Sits in the Driver's Seat of the All-New Tesla Model Y L, Lets the Car Drive on Its Own
20 photos
Photo: Jay Leno's Garage | YouTube
Three rows, six seats, two motors, and six inches of extra legroom. This is the all-new Tesla Model Y L. The electric SUV went into production at Giga Texas back in September, and deliveries have just begun. That is the exact car that Jay Leno takes for a drive, but he doesn’t actually drive it.
The car that has just been parked in Jay Leno's Garage is a 2027 Tesla Model Y L with the Premium trim, finished in Cosmic Silver, a new exterior color, over a Zen Gray interior, which is a new interior color, and rides on 20-inch wheels.
It is one of the few hundred units that Tesla is "releasing into the wild" bearing the Launch Edition badge. Lars Moravy, Vice President of Vehicle Engineering, and Franz von Holzhausen, Head of Design, accompany the car on the show to dissect it on camera.
Tesla has offered a three-row version of the Model Y before as a $2,500 factory upgrade, but with no wheelbase extension, as the automaker squeezed two more seats into the existing trunk space, in which two adults could have only traveled in terribly contorted positions. As for the L version, it is not just a stretched version of the standard model.
Photo: Jay Leno's Garage | YouTube Now, the extended-wheelbase Tesla Model Y L is roughly 7 inches (179 millimeters) longer, which translates to 6 more inches of interior space. That makes enough space for two adults to travel comfortably in the third row.
That is also because the extended-wheelbase variant features a straightened rear quarter-panel roofline to maximize headroom in the back, a spoiler-integrated brake light, and a lower drag coefficient: 0.216 versus 0.220 for the standard model. This configuration is what Lars Moravy’s sister-in-law has been asking for long before it came out.
The Model Y L comes with a dual-motor powertrain pushing out 496 horsepower (503 metric horsepower) and 405 pound-feet (493 Newton meters) of torque. That is enough to make it flash from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in 4.4 seconds on its way to a top speed of 125 mph (201 kph). " Because you know we don't make slow cars, " Moravy brags.
An upgraded 83-kWh NMCA battery pack allows the vehicle to handle the extra 212 pounds of structural weight from the elongated wheelbase without sacrificing the brisk acceleration characteristic of the standard lineup.
Photo: Jay Leno's Garage | YouTube The battery stores enough energy for a drive of up to 332 miles (534 kilometers) before it needs to be plugged in again, when it rides on 19-inch wheels. When equipped with the 20-inch wheels, like this car is, it goes as far as 328 miles (528 kilometers) on a single charge .
Tesla has officially crossed the 10 million vehicle milestone at its Fremont, California factory. The milestone car was a black Model Y. Out of Tesla's 10.2 million vehicles delivered, the Tesla Model Y has surpassed 4.5 million lifetime sales globally.
With ten airbags and Full Self-Driving , the Model Y L, just like its siblings, stands as one of the safest cars out there. Once in the driver’s seat, Jay Leno doesn't need to touch anything. The car drives on its own, with no human interference whatsoever. But he does need to pay attention, because the system tracks the user’s eyesight through an integrated cabin-facing camera located directly above the rearview mirror.
The system continuously tracks your eyes to calculate where you are looking. If you glance away from the windshield to look at your phone, interact extensively with the center screen, or stare out the side windows, the system registers the divergence.
Photo: Jay Leno's Garage | YouTube In addition to eye gaze, the camera also evaluates the angle and tilt of your head to check for drowsiness or medical emergencies, monitoring if your head begins to droop. When FSD uses the vision system to gauge attention, a green indicator appears in the status bar on the main screen to show that camera monitoring is active.
For Tesla, putting the self-driving tech from the Cybercab in all of its vehicles is just a matter of time. " I have not touched the steering wheel since we left the garage," Leno admits. Lars Moravy says he traveled just like that for a record 80 miles (129 kilometers).
Now, with Leno in the driver's seat, the car pulls over to make room for an ambulance to pass, reacting far better than other drivers who don't move out of the way just as fast. However, a DUI is still a DUI in any Tesla, except for the Cybercab . The responsibility lies with the driver.
From the captain’s chair in the second row, the ride is more comfortable, with generous legroom and an integrated, fold-down padded armrest on the inside edge, mirroring the premium seating style found in the larger Model X.
Photo: Jay Leno's Garage | YouTube Both second-row seats feature multi-stage heating, integrated USB-C fast-charging ports built into the rear of the center console, and localized air vents connected to the vehicle's upgraded three-zone climate control system.
At some point, Leno asks about “a new S-Class,” actually referring to the Model S, but the final one rolled off the production line two months ago with no successor in sight. However, it is a never-say-never situation, Lars Moravy admits. But is there really a need or a demand for a sedan when you’ve got all you need in an SUV?
That one SUV that checks all the boxes starts at $61,990 in Launch Edition form. That is roughly $4,000 above the standard Model Y Performance ($57,990) and about $12,000 above a standard Model Y Long Range AWD.
